story.name: トウキョウ ひとりぐらし
story.title: Under the Harvest Moon
story.line: ブーケが みんなと おつきみを します
story.ja: 9月の終わり、東京に来てもうすぐ1か月。ごみの日も、おにぎりの開け方もわかるようになり、もう地図もいらない。職場のチッチから、今夜は十五夜、お月見の日だと聞く。それに、引っ越したらご近所にあいさつの品を持っていくものだとも。あわてたブーケは、コンビニでレムから最後の月見だんごを買い、お菓子の箱と紺色の傘を持ってアリゲッティのもとへ。アリゲッティはお菓子を受け取り、傘は「もうあなたの傘。ノックする理由になるでしょ」と返す。夜は川ぞいの小さな公園で、たぬきち、チッチ、休憩中のレムといっしょにお月見。月のうさぎがもちをついているのが見えた。「時がたつのは早いわね。来年はあなたが、新しい人に傘を貸す番よ」。

segments.en: By the end of September, Rosie had been in Tokyo for almost a month. She knew, because she had been crossing off the days on her calendar.
She knew a lot of things now. Burnable trash on Tuesdays and Fridays. Pull number one, then two, then three. Wash first, then soak.
She knew which vending machine had hot corn soup, and which bakery had melon bread at four o'clock. She didn't need the map anymore.
On Friday afternoon, at the studio, Nana leaned over the little wall between their desks.
Hey, tonight's the harvest moon. It's kind of a thing here. You look at the moon, eat little white rice dumplings, and just hang out.
Oh, and when you move in somewhere, you're supposed to bring your neighbors a little gift. Like a box of sweets. Did you do that?
A gift? When you move in? No! Nobody told me! It's been a whole month! And Gayle has done so much for me.
So on the way home, Rosie stopped at the sweet shop by the station, and then at the convenience store, where Sherb was just starting his shift.
Moon dumplings? Yeah, we've got them. You're lucky. Last two boxes. Are you having a party or something?
Rosie bought both boxes, and just in case.
That evening, she knocked on Gayle's door with a box of sweets, the big navy umbrella, and a very red face.
Gayle, I'm so sorry. I just found out I was supposed to bring you a gift when I moved in. So, here. A month late.
And here's your umbrella. Finally. Thank you for lending it to me.
Oh, Rosie. You shouldn't have. You watered my tomatoes. You came to the bath with me. That's better than any box of sweets.
Gayle took the sweets. Then she looked at the umbrella for a moment, and gently pushed it back into Rosie's hands.
No, you keep this one. It knows the way to your door now. And any time you need a reason to knock, you'll have one.
Rosie didn't trust herself to say anything. So she just gave her a hug, umbrella and all.
Later, when it was dark, they met at the little park by the river. Tom Nook brought folding chairs. Nana brought a thermos of tea.
And Sherb came over on his break, still in his uniform, with a bag of snacks the store was about to throw away.
What a night! Not a single cloud. Yes, yes. You know, Rosie, people here say there's a rabbit in the moon, making rice cakes. Look closely.
A rabbit? Really? Where? Back home, people say there's a face. The man in the moon.
Look at the dark parts. There are his long ears. There's his little hammer. And there, that's the bowl he makes the rice cakes in.
Oh! I see it! I actually see it! Now I'm never going to be able to unsee that.
They ate the dumplings, which were soft and chewy and only a little bit sweet. Sherb ate four. Nobody said anything.
So? One month. How does it feel? Honestly.
Honestly? On my first night, I sat on the floor and talked to my apartment. I was so lonely.
And now look. I have a neighbor, and a landlord, and a coworker, and a convenience store guy.
Hey, I'm not just the convenience store guy. I'm also the goldfish guy.
And a goldfish guy. And a goldfish. And a bath on Thursdays. I think I really live here now.
Time flies, doesn't it? You'll see. Next year, you'll be the one lending an umbrella to somebody new.
When the tea was gone, everybody said good night and went home, one by one, down the little streets by the river.
Rosie climbed the stairs, said good night to Mochi, and stood the big navy umbrella by her door. Her umbrella now.
Then she called her mom, who was just having breakfast back in Ohio, and told her all about the rabbit.
Outside, the moon was high and white over the river. And the whole neighborhood was asleep under it. Goodnight.

ph.ja: ちょっとした恒例なの
